objective: Spend the next candidate answers on historical situations where changing model is plausible. Compare targeted acquisition and automatic stopping with a balanced 200-question embedding trained on the same history.
data: Separate 1,600 previously unused canonical groups from the remaining historical bank with seed 52419, stratified to the original five-task mixture. Exclude these groups, the preceding 2,556-question reserve, every seed's original 200-question panel, and all earlier evaluation groups from the shared decoder. Refit full upstream TextMF after excluding all 1,600 new groups. Use fresh outcomes only after fixing this design.
protocol: A common 80-question balanced warm-up identifies two historical peers. Sample further questions uniformly within the five-source/four-state cells. Allocate batches of 40 toward cells that matter for close decisions on ungraded development prompts and have high paired outcome variance. Reweight the candidate embedding for the population prevalence of each observed cell. Compare fixed 200 and a policy that may stop at 120 or 160 when the estimated maximum remaining improvement is below 0.2 percentage points.
predictions: Fit the same 95-dimensional candidate representation and the same eight-helper joint state estimator. Controls are balanced 200, matched panel-fixed choice, and the full-data original restricted to these known IDs. The three panel seeds stay separate. Record exact acquired prompt IDs and stop reasons; select no threshold or seed on the new sample. Results on earlier questions are secondary.
